Photograph: Dave Decker/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock US midterm elections 2026 Democratic socialist Angie Nixon clinches surprise primary win in Florida US Senate race Nixon bested Alexander Vindman to win Democratic nomination and now faces Republican Ashley Moody in November Trump-backed Byron Donalds wins Republican primary in race to succeed Florida governor DeSantis Richard Luscombe Tue 18 Aug 2026 20.26 EDT Last modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 20.48 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google In an upset for the Democratic establishment, progressive Angie Nixon won the party’s US Senate primary in Florida , beating former army intelligence officer Alexander Vindman. Nixon, a state representative and member of the Democratic Socialists of America, had significantly less funding going into the primary – with $975,000 to Vindman’s $16.3m at the end of July, according to Florida Politics . Vindman was previously better known for being a whistleblower leading to Trump’s first impeachment in 2019 after the US president sought to withhold military aid to Ukraine. Democrats have their sights set on upsetting Republican Ashley Moody in the US Senate general election. Moody, picked by DeSantis to replace Marco Rubio when he became secretary of state last year, won what was almost a token primary election to run in November to serve the remaining two years of Rubio’s term. https://telex.hu/kulfold/2026/10/16/ukra.text: Menü Kereső Ukrán külügyminiszter: Magyar Péter bölcs hozzáállással elérte azt, amit Orbán zsarolással soha Külföld Nyilas Gergely Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Magyar Péter és Volodimir Zelenszkij első tárgyalása után méltatta a két ország látványosan javuló kapcsolatát az ukrán külügyminiszter is, reagálva Orbán Anita nem sokkal korábbi, szintén pozitív hangvételű bejegyzésére , amelyben a magyar külügyminiszter kijelentette, hogy a két ország vezetése a teljes magyar–ukrán kapcsolatrendszer megújításán dolgozik. Andrij Szibiha válaszul kitért arra, hogy a magyar kormányfő és az ukrán elnök pénteki találkozója mellett a külügyminiszteri szintű tárgyalást is megtartották, amely hozzájárul a kapcsolatok új alapokra helyezéséhez, „gazdasági, humanitárius, politikai és egyéb téren”. „Sok területen van még tennivalónk, de már egyértelműen kimondhatjuk: ez egy új fejezet. Történelmi. Közösen bebizonyítottuk, hogy a nyugodt diplomácia kölcsönösen kifizetődő. […] Magyar Péter miniszterelnök és csapata néhány hónap alatt elérte azt bölcs, együttműködő hozzáállással, amit Orbán Viktor képtelen volt elérni éveken át tartó zsarolással” – jelentette ki Szibiha, a gazdasági, infrastrukturális, határokon átívelő együttműködés megvalósításának, az „erősebb Európa” közös építésének fontosságát kiemelve. A diplomata szintén kitért arra, hogy a kormányközi bizottságok folytatják a kétoldalú munkát „a kölcsönösen gyümölcsöző együttműködés érdekében”, mert a két ország „megérdemli a jószomszédi kapcsolatokat, és a közös jövőt a békés Európában”. https://www.politico.eu/article/some-oil.text: BRUSSELS — Some of the world's biggest oil companies will be able to promote themselves as green investments in the EU under an overhaul of the bloc's sustainable finance rules. EU member countries and lawmakers struck a deal late Thursday to update the Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation that will make it easier for private investment earmarked for green activities to flow into new fossil fuel projects. It was Big Oil's second big European win of the day, after the EU agreed early Thursday to delay methane emission rules for fossil fuel companies for two years. Advertisement Advertisement The sustainable finance agreement substantially loosens a proposal by the European Commission to get more money flowing into companies that are switching from dirtier to cleaner business models. The executive decided to overhaul the SFDR, which aims to prevent greenwashing and help investors make sustainable investment decisions, last November. It proposed introducing three new categories for green funds — ESG basics, Transition and Sustainable — which each have progressively stricter sustainability criteria. EU countries and the European Parliament had disagreed over whether fossil fuel companies should be allowed in the new "transition" category. The Commission proposed a blanket exclusion, but member countries pushed for oil companies with greener ambitions to be included. The Parliament, meanwhile, only wanted oil and gas companies to be allowed if they invest more in green activities than in new oil and gas projects over a three-year period. Under Thursday's final agreement, seen by POLITICO, the EU has ruled that companies will have to spend one-fifth of their capital expenditure on green activities and this will have to “meaningfully” increase “over time” and be measured annually. The increase in green investment cannot be “merely marginal or nominal,” the rules specified. The 20% capex threshold will be reviewed by the Commission in five years. Advertisement Advertisement Companies will also have to produce a Paris-aligned emissions reduction plan for some of their emissions. However, downstream emissions — which represent the biggest share of oil and gas companies’ emissions — will not have to be covered by these plans. The EU’s finance chief, Maria Luís Albuquerque, told POLITICO that the final deal was “close enough” to the Commission’s proposal as she left the meeting. The outcome could see big oil and gas companies like France’s TotalEnergies and Spain’s Repsol qualify for financing under the transition category, based on their 2025 capital expenditure. The French oil giant met with the lead Parliament negotiator, Dutch MEP Gerben-Jan Gerbrandy, three times between the start of 2025 and June 2026, according to Parliament documents . Aleksandra Palinska, executive director at sustainable finance trade association Eurosif, said the criteria agreed by the co-legislators on the transition category “fail to distinguish companies genuinely transforming their business models from those making isolated green investments.” Capitals win EU capitals proposed a more lenient approach than the Commission and Parliament, agreeing in June that Big Oil could be included in the transition category if companies spend one-fifth of their capital expenditure on green activities, as defined under the EU taxonomy on sustainable investments. Advertisement Advertisement This is despite several EU countries advocating for a move away from fossil fuels and publishing fossil fuel phase-out plans at COP31 this month. Lawmakers in October voted for big oil and gas companies to only be included in the category if they invest more in green activities than in new fossil fuel projects over a three-year period. Several EU countries — including France and Italy — saw the Parliament’s position as a “red line,” according to a document seen by POLITICO, with the final agreement landing closer to what EU capitals wanted. Despite this, Gerbrandy, who led negotiations in Parliament, said he was happy with the agreement. “I think we achieved a result that is in accordance with the criteria I set — credibility and administrative burdens — so I’m very satisfied,” he said.
